finale.title: Port Jefferson Ferry
finale.subtitle: Long Island Sound crossing to Bridgeport, Connecticut
finale.closingLine: Nine pieces of the harbor — one ferry still ties Long Island to Connecticut.

checkpoints.name: Shipbuilders Memorial
checkpoints.blurb: Harborfront Park’s landmark sculpture honors the shipbuilders who framed Port Jefferson’s working waterfront.
facts: The sculpture shows builders carrying a hull frame toward the harbor.
Harborfront Park replaced earlier industrial waterfront uses, including oil terminal land.

checkpoints.name: Ferry Terminal
checkpoints.blurb: The Bridgeport & Port Jefferson ferry terminal is the village’s living bridge across Long Island Sound.
facts: Ferries connect Port Jefferson, NY to Bridgeport, CT.
The terminal sits on West Broadway at the harbor’s edge.

checkpoints.name: Bayles Shipyard
checkpoints.blurb: Bayles Shipyard is a National Register site — chandlery, machine shop, and mould loft that powered a shipbuilding village.
facts: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2000.
The 1917 machine shop and mould loft later anchored civic harbor reuse.

checkpoints.name: Historical Society Museum
checkpoints.blurb: The Mather House Museum complex keeps Port Jefferson’s shipbuilding and village stories in one hillside campus.
facts: Headquarters of the Historical Society of Greater Port Jefferson.
Outbuildings include a tool shed, sail loft collections, and period shop recreations.

checkpoints.name: Village Center
checkpoints.blurb: The Village Center turns former shipyard fabric into a public harbor hub.
facts: Civic programming and gatherings sit where industry once dominated the shoreline.

checkpoints.name: Main Street
checkpoints.blurb: Main Street is the everyday village spine between the hills and the harbor.
facts: Shops and sidewalks frame how most visitors first meet downtown Port Jefferson.

checkpoints.name: Waterfront Dining
checkpoints.blurb: Harbor dining is part of Port Jeff’s welcome — tables facing the same water the ferry crosses.
facts: Waterfront restaurants and inns cluster along the Broadway harbor edge.

checkpoints.name: Drowned Meadow Cottage Museum
checkpoints.blurb: Drowned Meadow Cottage remembers an earlier landscape before the modern downtown filled the meadow.
facts: A compact museum stop that deepens the village story beyond the postcard harbor.

checkpoints.name: Harbor Overlook
checkpoints.blurb: From the overlook, Long Island Sound opens — the path the ferry still takes to Connecticut.
facts: Sightlines across the harbor reconnect park, shipyard memory, and the ferry route.
